Link ATAC peaks to paired measured expression

Source: R/RunLinkPeaks.R
RunLinkPeaks.Rd

Run native Signac peak-gene correlation and matched-background testing on paired RNA and ATAC assays, retaining native link statistics.

Usage

RunLinkPeaks(
  object,
  assay = NULL,
  expression.assay = "RNA",
  peak.slot = "counts",
  expression.slot = "data",
  method = "pearson",
  gene.coords = NULL,
  distance = 5e+05,
  min.distance = NULL,
  min.cells = 10L,
  genes.use = NULL,
  n.sample = 200L,
  pvalue.cutoff = 0.05,
  score.cutoff = 0.05,
  gene.id = FALSE,
  seed = 11L,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A Seurat object containing paired chromatin and measured RNA assays. Identical cell names must identify the same biological cells. RNA must cover all cells of the selected ATAC assay; additional RNA-only cells are retained but excluded from this calculation. Missing pairs are rejected.

assay

Chromatin assay; defaults to the active assay.

expression.assay

Measured RNA assay, default "RNA". Gene activity, imputed expression and chromVAR scores are not measured RNA.

peak.slot, expression.slot

Single existing native layers, default "counts" and "data". Split layers must be joined explicitly beforehand.

method

Correlation method, "pearson" or "spearman".

gene.coords

Optional native gene-coordinate GRanges passed to Signac::LinkPeaks(). With NULL, native Signac collapses assay transcript annotation. Coordinates must declare the same genome label as the assay; known chromosome lengths must agree. Explicit coordinates require one interval per gene identity. No chromosome-style conversion is performed.

distance

Maximum genomic distance to TSS in bases, default 500000.

min.distance

Optional non-negative minimum distance to TSS.

min.cells

Native strict detection threshold: peaks and genes must occur in more than this many cells, default 10.

genes.use

Optional unique RNA feature IDs to test.

n.sample

Number of matched background peaks, default 200.

pvalue.cutoff, score.cutoff

Native strict p-value and absolute correlation thresholds, default 0.05. P-values are native unadjusted normal-tail values pnorm(-abs(zscore)), without a two-tail multiplier or multiple-testing correction; they are not adjusted significance estimates.

gene.id

Whether RNA feature IDs match annotation gene_id rather than gene_name, default FALSE. Use TRUE for ReadMultiomeData() gene IDs.

seed

Random seed used locally for native background sampling.

verbose

Whether to print progress messages.

Value

The Seurat object with native Signac::Links(object[[assay]]) and a receipt at Misc(object[[assay]], "scop_link_peaks"), recording source assays, layers, cells, input features, parameters, backend version and the number of retained links. Native link metadata contains gene, peak, score, zscore and pvalue for non-empty results. Links are associations, not causal or experimentally verified regulatory connections.

Details

Run Signac RegionStats with an appropriate genome sequence before this function; finite GC.percent between 0 and 100 and sequence.length equal to peak width are required. These metadata checks do not verify the supplied DNA provenance. Native accessibility background counts are recomputed on the paired cells in a temporary assay, avoiding stale count metadata after cell subsetting. Background sampling, correlation, z scores and significance filtering are delegated unchanged to Signac. Its minimum support and chromosome-background requirements still apply. Source counts and the active assay are preserved. Existing native links or SCOP link results are never overwritten. No retained links is a valid empty result, not evidence that regulation is absent. Native errors for constant expression or insufficient background support are preserved; no alternative correlation or significance model is substituted.

See also

ReadMultiomeData(), Signac::LinkPeaks(), Signac::RegionStats()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("Signac", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("Biostrings", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("BSgenome", quietly = TRUE)) {
  local({
    withr::local_preserve_seed()
    set.seed(83)
    counts <- Matrix::Matrix(matrix(rpois(60 * 40, 4) + 1, 60,
      dimnames = list(paste0("p", 1:60), paste0("cell", 1:40))
    ), sparse = TRUE)
    ranges <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
      seqnames = rep(c("chr1", "chr2"), each = 30),
      start = rep(seq(1, by = 200, length.out = 30), 2),
      end = rep(seq(100, by = 200, length.out = 30), 2)
    ))
    paired <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = ranges, genome = "toy", verbose = FALSE)
    rna <- counts[c(1, 31), , drop = FALSE]
    rownames(rna) <- c("g1", "g2")
    paired[["RNA"]] <- SeuratObject::CreateAssayObject(counts = rna)
    genes <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
      seqnames = c("chr1", "chr2"), start = 201, end = 400, strand = "+",
      gene_id = c("g1", "g2"), gene_name = c("g1", "g2")
    ), keep.extra.columns = TRUE)
    GenomeInfoDb::genome(genes) <- "toy"
    # Small synthetic sequence solely for an executable method example.
    dna <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(setNames(vapply(
      1:2, function(i) {
        paste(sample(c("A", "C", "G", "T"), 6000, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")
      },
      character(1)
    ), c("chr1", "chr2")))
    paired <- Signac::RegionStats(paired, assay = "peaks", genome = dna, verbose = FALSE)
    linked <- RunLinkPeaks(paired,
      assay = "peaks", expression.slot = "counts",
      gene.coords = genes, min.cells = 0, n.sample = 10, distance = 10000,
      pvalue.cutoff = 1, verbose = FALSE
    )
    Signac::Links(linked[["peaks"]])
  })
}
